description.narrative: After the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, all coastal states automatically have the right to the continental shelf. This shelf extends a minimum of 200 nautical miles. Shelf beyond 200 nautical miles must be documented to the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf. Coastal states have ten years to present such documentation. From 2008 to 2014, Norway assisted Cape Verde, Mauritania, Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Sierra Leone in the work of documenting the outer limit of their continental shelves beyond 200 nautical miles. The project was led by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The technical aspects were carried out and coordinated by GRID-Arendal and the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate. The technical part also included a very large data collection program funded by Norway. The project, called the Continental Shelf Initiative, resulted in the countries submitting a joint data presentation to the Commission in 2014. The Shelf Commission currently has 30 presentations on the waiting list before West Africa's. Therefore, a waiting time of 4-7 years for commission processing is expected. In the meantime, it is important to maintain necessary shelf competence in these states so that they can defend the shelf submission to the Commission. To meet this need, the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate has held annual workshops since 2017, financed by Norway, where all countries participate with their technical experts to update themselves on developments in the relevant fields, new data becoming available, and the potential development of precedents in the Commission's published recommendations. It has been shown that all professionals from the old network attended, and the professional updates and discussions were therefore very effective. All participants and the secretariat in Cape Verde consider such workshops to be a good tool for maintaining both competence and networks and have expressed a strong desire for continuation.
